title: Domain-specific prompt curation protocol for quantization calibration packs
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Goal: Define a repeatable, privacy-preserving protocol to curate per-domain calibration packs used for FP8 and INT8 quantization profile generation and accuracy validation. The protocol must produce compact packs (~5k-50k prompts per domain depending on traffic) that preserve representative activation distributions seen in production for both short and long context workloads. The output will feed the calibration pipeline (activation percentile collection, dynamic range estimation) and the accuracy validation harness (logit/regression testing and downstream-task evaluation).
acceptance_criteria: A set of domain calibration packs (chat, search, code, finance, healthcare) generated by the protocol exists in the calibration bucket with immutable versioned paths
Calibration packs achieve KL divergence on token logits < 0.03 relative to production sample baseline for top-50 tokens across domains when evaluated on FP32 vs FP8 simulated quantization
End-to-end quantization pipelines accept per-domain packs without manual tuning for >= 80% of nightly calibration runs
Privacy guards (PII masking and pattern removal) are applied and documented; a review signoff from Security is attached
Sampling metadata (seed, embedding model, cluster IDs, timestamps) is emitted for reproducibility
proposed_sampling_strategy: Hybrid traffic + semantic exemplar sampling. Steps: 1) Ingest raw production prompts for the target domain over a rolling 30-day window with per-customer sampling caps to avoid skew. 2) Apply light normalization and canonicalization (strip session ids, timestamps, random tokens) and run a configurable PII scrubber. 3) Compute 1536-d embeddings using the stable-embed-v2 model, then cluster with HDBSCAN to identify semantic modes. 4) For each cluster, apply dual-stage selection: (a) reservoir sampling with a recency TTL weight to bias newer high-frequency patterns, and (b) exemplar selection by maximizing pairwise token-level activation variance estimated from a small FP32 probe pass (10% of cluster samples). 5) Enforce per-length stratification (short <32, medium 32-256, long >256 tokens) and per-candidate-kv-cache usage tag. 6) Deduplicate near-duplicates via normalized hash and enforce a 1% maximum duplicate allowance. 7) Cap pack size per domain and tier by traffic percentiles; keep heavy-hitter prompts as pinned exemplars for stability. This approach balances coverage of rare modes and high-volume patterns while keeping pack sizes bounded.
calibration_pack_format: JSONL per-example with fields: id, domain, timestamp, normalized_prompt, embedding_id, cluster_id, length_bucket, probe_activation_signature (base64), privacy_masking_version, source_bucket, sampling_seed, provenance_link. Each pack is compressed (.gz) and accompanied by a manifest (CSV) that lists distribution histograms for token lengths, cluster sizes, and per-layer activation percentiles (p1,p5,p25,p50,p75,p95,p99).
validation_plan: Two-stage validation: unit-level and system-level. Unit: run simulated quantization (FP32 -> fake-FP8/int8) on a held-out subset and compute: token-logit KL divergence, mean squared error of pre-softmax logits, perplexity delta, and top-1/top-5 exact-match on task-specific evals. System: run the full calibration (scale/zero-point estimation, per-channel ranges) and then run nightly regression suite comprising: nLU intent accuracy, code-generation pass-rate on fuzzed tests, and reranking NDCG. Define thresholds: KL < 0.03, MSE < 0.002 on logits, downstream accuracy drop < 1.5% absolute. Any domain exceeding thresholds triggers automatic rollback and opens ENG rollback incident linking the pack version. Evaluation artifacts are stored in evaluation dashboards with links in the manifest.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Dry run: generate packs for 2 low-risk domains (docs-assistant, internal-search) and validate in nightly simulation cluster
Stage 1 - Canary: deploy calibration profile derived from per-domain pack to a 5% traffic canary on dedicated GPU pools with telemetry on latency, error rate, and output-quality metrics
Stage 2 - Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 75% over 48-hour windows if no regressions; otherwise halt and investigate
Stage 3 - Full rollout: promote profile to all eligible Serving runtime instances and mark pack as stable in release manifest
privacy_and_compliance_notes: PII scrubber v3 will remove emails, SSNs, credit card patterns and mask model-specific secrets. Customer sampling caps enforce per-customer max 0.1% of prompts carried into any pack. Audit log of original keys is stored in an encrypted SSM-only bucket with access via an approved SR. Security signoff required before canary.
ops_and_infrastructure_requirements: Calibration pack generator runs as a batch job in the data-platform namespace; needs 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM, GPU optional for probe activation runs. Output written to s3://redwood-calib/domain-packs/{domain}/{version}/. CI task to verify manifest checksums and activation percentile summaries before signing packs for rollout.
notes: We opted against pure reservoir sampling because it underweights rare but semantically important modes discovered in embeddings clustering.
Embedding model choice has measurable effect on cluster granularity; we'll include model version in manifest and re-run older packs if embed model changes more than two minor versions.
Consider adding synthetic paraphrase augmentation for low-traffic domains to increase calibration signal for rare intent forms.
